text:
alex: heads-up — saw a pod on cpu-only nodes this morning even though the chart sets tolerations for gpu nodes. looks like the helm helper that merges node-level defaults with workload overrides is dropping arrays when overlay has an empty string.

maria: ugh. which helper? the chart has that generic merge helper in _helpers.tpl right?

alex: yep. helper does a `fromYaml` + `merge` pattern. reproducer: in values.yaml we set `tolerations: \n  - key: nvidia.com/gpu\n    operator: Exists\n` but our infra overlay accidentally set `tolerations: ""` (string). the merge logic converts that to an empty scalar and ends up with no tolerations in final manifest.

ravi: CI lint flagged a schema issue earlier: `values.schema.json: expected array but found string` on one PR, but it was dismissed as flaky. maybe that was the same root cause.

ci-bot: helm-lint: ERROR: values.schema.json: path "/workloads/*/tolerations" - expected type array, got string at index 0

sophia: that matches. our overlay generator (the kustomize/templating step in infra CD) sometimes writes empty-string for absent lists to avoid deleting keys, which is a terrible hack.

alex: suggested fixes: (1) make the helper defensive: if `kind` != "array" then fallback to creating an empty array before merging. (2) tighten values.schema.json so PRs fail fast (no dismissed flaky warnings). (3) add an integration unit test in the helm-unittest harness that runs `helm template` with an overlay that sets empty-string and assert tolerations present.

maria: +1. for (1) can we do a small helper like `ensureArray`? example:```{{- define "ensureArray" -}}
{{- $v := . | fromYaml }}
{{- if eq (kindIs $v "array") true }}{{- $v }}{{- else }}[]{{- end }}
{{- end }}
``` But we need to use the right sprig/helm helpers — `kindIs` expects an object from `toJson`? need to test.

ravi: Another quick fix: in the overlay generator, write `tolerations: []` instead of empty string. that will stop the conversion problem before helm sees it. ops-bot: can we change infra generator?

ops-bot: I'll open a change to the overlay tool to emit explicit empty arrays for known list fields (tolerations, tolerationsPatch, env, args). rolling patch to infra repo now.

sophia: also saw an unrelated `batchSize` regression — schema expects integer but default is `"16"` in one microchart. helm template doesn't always error and later code in the runtime parses it and crashes. we should add schema rules for these numeric fields too.

alex: agreed. action items: 1) ops-bot change overlay generator (ops-bot will PR). 2) eng-platform add `ensureArray` helper + unit test (maria + ravi pair). 3) update values.schema.json to mark `tolerations` as array and `batchSize` as integer and enable CI to block on those schema failures (sophia). 4) enable helm-unittest case in pipeline.

maria: I'll take the helper + tests. will add a small fixture in charts/*/tests/ that uses the empty-string overlay to prove the helper.

ravi: I'll audit other charts for stringified numbers/arrays with a quick grep and put a checklist in the PR.

ci-bot: Note: adding stricter schema will cause some older deploys to fail if overlays still use the hacks. consider a one-week grace with warnings in the CI to notify consumers before hard-blocking.

sophia: good call — ops-bot can roll a notifier job that scans open overlays and posts to #help with list of offending PRs.

ops-bot: created PR infra/overlay-fix -> main to emit explicit arrays for known list fields. will add issue to onboard teams. PR: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/overlay-fix (link placeholder). :shipit:

alex: thanks folks. once infra PR merges i'll bump the helm tests and we can watch CI for first failures next week. :eyes:
